text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of DVT and long-standing swelling, I suspect chronic venous insufficiency. Does the wound have irregular edges and exudate, and do you experience relief for the swelling when you elevate your leg?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient has not answered my specific questions regarding wound characteristics or elevation relief, but the history of DVT, chronic swelling, and family history strongly points to venous etiology. text: RESULTS: Doppler_Ultrasound_Lower_Limb: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms significant venous reflux and obstruction, which directly supports the diagnosis of chronic venous insufficiency leading to a venous stasis ulcer. Given the strong clinical picture and confirmatory imaging, I am ready to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer
